title: Yengema and Kamabai Archaeological Finds
summary: Archaeological excavations at Yengema cave and Kamabai rock shelter revealed stone tools, quartz artifacts, and early pottery.
description: Archaeological excavations conducted by Carleton Coon and later researchers at Yengema Cave (Kono District) and Kamabai Rock Shelter (Bombali District) provided concrete material evidence of human habitation in Sierra Leone dating to the Upper Stone Age and Neolithic transition. Finds included quartz microliths, ground stone axes, and early ceramics, illustrating long-term human adaptation to the West African rainforest ecosystem prior to iron technology.

title: Naming of 'Serra Leoa' by Pedro de Sintra
summary: Portuguese navigator Pedro de Sintra chartered the mountainous coast and gave it the name 'Serra Leoa'.
description: In 1462, Portuguese navigator Pedro de Sintra sailed into the natural harbor formed by the Sierra Leone Peninsula. Struck by the towering, lion-like contours of the mountains or the roar of thunderstorms across the peaks, he recorded the region as 'Serra Leoa' (Lion Mountains). This mark on European portolan charts opened a long period of coastal trade in ivory, timber, and captives between indigenous rulers and European merchants.

title: Construction and Expansion of Bunce Island Slave Castle
summary: Bunce Island became a principal British slave-trading depot supplying captives, especially rice farmers, to the Americas.
description: Established by the Gambia Adventurers and later managed by the Royal African Company and Grant, Oswald & Company, Bunce Island in the Sierra Leone River was fortified with heavy artillery. Thousands of enslaved Africans captured across the Windward Coast were held in dungeons before transport across the Atlantic. Slave owners in South Carolina and Georgia specifically sought captives from Sierra Leone due to their expert knowledge of rice cultivation.

title: Arrival of the Black Poor and Founding of Granville Town
summary: British abolitionists organized the settlement of over 400 Black Poor from London in Granville Town.
description: In May 1787, ships carrying over 400 impoverished Black people from London (many freed from American Revolutionary War service or domestic servitude) arrived under the guidance of British abolitionist Granville Sharp. Land was acquired from local Koya Temne chief King Naimbana. Though disease, climate, and disputes devastated the initial settlement at Granville Town, it laid the direct institutional precursor for Freetown.

title: Arrival of Nova Scotian Settlers & Founding of Freetown
summary: 1,196 Black Loyalists from Nova Scotia arrived in 15 ships, founding the town of Freetown.
description: Led by Thomas Peters and John Clarkson under the auspices of the Sierra Leone Company, 1,196 Black Loyalists—African Americans who fought for the British in the American War of Independence in exchange for freedom—sailed from Halifax, Nova Scotia. Upon landing at the peninsula, they sang hymns, cleared the forest, and founded Freetown, establishing democratic town meetings, churches, and civic institutions.

title: Arrival of Jamaican Maroons
summary: Over 500 Jamaican Maroons deported after the Second Maroon War arrived and settled Maroon Town in Freetown.
description: After resisting British forces in Jamaica during the Second Maroon War, over 500 Maroons were exiled to Nova Scotia and subsequently transported to Freetown in September 1800. Arriving during a rebellion by earlier Nova Scotian settlers against Sierra Leone Company rule, the Maroons assisted Company forces in restoring order, receiving land grants in what became Maroon Town.

title: Establishment of British Crown Colony of Sierra Leone
summary: Sierra Leone Company surrendered governance to the British Crown, making Freetown a Crown Colony.
description: Facing financial instability and armed pressure from surrounding indigenous polities, the Sierra Leone Company transferred its administrative authority to the British Crown on January 1, 1808. Freetown became the headquarters for the British Royal Navy's West Africa Squadron sent to enforce the Abolition of the Slave Trade Act (1807), leading to the liberation of tens of thousands of captive Africans.

title: Founding of Fourah Bay College
summary: Church Missionary Society established Fourah Bay College, earning Freetown the title 'Athens of West Africa'.
description: The Church Missionary Society (CMS) established Fourah Bay College at Cline Town, Freetown, as an institution for training African clergymen, teachers, and administrators. Samuel Ajayi Crowther was its first student. Affiliated with Durham University in 1876, FBC became the first Western university-level institution in West Africa, drawing scholars from Nigeria, Ghana, the Gambia, and across the continent.

title: Declaration of British Protectorate Over Hinterland
summary: Britain declared a Protectorate over the interior, dividing Sierra Leone legally between Colony and Protectorate.
description: Without treaty agreement or consent from hinterland paramount chiefs, Governor Sir Frederic Cardew proclaimed a British Protectorate over the interior of Sierra Leone. The proclamation introduced indirect rule, subordinated traditional rulers under District Commissioners, imposed colonial boundary lines, and prepared the groundwork for controversial direct taxation.

title: The 1898 Hut Tax War
summary: Paramount Chief Bai Bureh and southern Mende leaders led armed uprisings against colonial hut taxes.
description: In response to Governor Cardew's five-shilling annual 'hut tax' imposed on indigenous dwellings, Temne chief Bai Bureh launched a sophisticated guerrilla warfare resistance in the north. Simultaneously, Mende and Sherbro communities in the south rose against colonial authorities, trading posts, and colonial officials. British forces executed heavy military campaigns, capturing Bai Bureh in November 1898 and exiling him to the Gold Coast.

title: Discovery of Diamonds in Kono District
summary: Geological Survey of Sierra Leone discovered rich alluvial diamond deposits in the Gbonkor stream.
description: Geologist J.D. Pollett discovered alluvial diamond deposits along the Gbonkor stream near Sefadu in Kono District. The British colonial administration subsequently granted exclusive mining monopoly rights to the Sierra Leone Selection Trust (SLST), owned by De Beers affiliate Consolidated African Selection Trust, initiating decades of legal and illicit diamond extraction that reshaped the economy.

title: Formation of Sierra Leone People's Party (SLPP)
summary: Dr. Milton Margai unified Protectorate leaders and educated elites to form the SLPP.
description: The Sierra Leone People's Party (SLPP) was established through the merger of the Sierra Leone Organization Society (SOS) and the People's Party. Led by Dr. Milton Margai, a medical doctor from Gbangbatoke, the SLPP campaigned under the motto 'One People, One Nation', seeking to bridge political divisions between the Crown Colony elites and Protectorate chiefdoms during decolonization negotiations.

title: Independence of Sierra Leone
summary: Sierra Leone achieved sovereign independence within the Commonwealth on 27 April 1961.
description: At midnight on 27 April 1961, the British Union Jack was lowered and the green, white, and blue flag of Sierra Leone was raised at Brookfields Stadium, Freetown. Sir Milton Margai became the first Prime Minister, with Queen Elizabeth II initially as constitutional monarch represented by Governor-General Sir Maurice Dorman. The nation entered the United Nations as its 100th member state.

title: 1967 Multi-Party Elections & Military Interventions
summary: Siaka Stevens won elections; military officers staged successive coups before returning democratic power.
description: In March 1967, the opposition All People's Congress (APC) led by Siaka Stevens defeated Sir Albert Margai's SLPP. Before Stevens could assume power, Army Commander Brigadier David Lansana intervened. Hours later, junior officers arrested Lansana and formed the National Reformation Council (NRC) under Andrew Juxon-Smith. In April 1968, Warrant Officer Patrick Bangura led a non-commissioned officers' revolt ('Anti-Corruption Revolutionary Movement') that restored Siaka Stevens to power.

title: Declaration of One-Party State Under APC
summary: President Siaka Stevens promulgated a new constitution declaring the APC the sole legal political party.
description: Following a national referendum criticized by opposition figures, President Siaka Stevens signed the 1978 Constitution into law, banning all opposition political parties, including the SLPP. All Members of Parliament were required to join the ruling All People's Congress (APC) within 24 hours or forfeit their seats, establishing 13 years of single-party authoritarian rule.

title: Invasion of Bomaru & Outbreak of Civil War
summary: Revolutionary United Front (RUF) launched armed attacks from Liberia, starting the Sierra Leone Civil War.
description: On 23 March 1991, fighters belonging to the Revolutionary United Front (RUF), led by former army corporal Foday Sankoh and supported by Charles Taylor's NPFL in Liberia, attacked the border town of Bomaru in Kailahun District. The conflict quickly spread into diamond-rich areas, precipitating an 11-year war characterized by severe civilian displacement, forced recruitment of child soldiers, and widespread atrocities.

title: NPRC Military Coup Led by Valentine Strasser
summary: Young army officers ousted President Joseph Momoh and formed the National Provisional Ruling Council.
description: Frustrated by non-payment of frontline salaries and poor equipment during the war against the RUF, 25-year-old Captain Valentine Strasser and junior officers drove to Freetown and forced President Joseph Saidu Momoh into exile in Guinea. They established the National Provisional Ruling Council (NPRC), suspending the constitution while declaring an intention to end the war and restore democracy.

title: Restoration of Multi-Party Democracy & Election of Ahmad Tejan Kabbah
summary: Ahmad Tejan Kabbah won presidential elections following the Bintumani I and II civil society conferences.
description: Driven by intense national civil society mobilization (National Consultative Conferences at Bintumani Hotel), military rule gave way to democratic elections. Ahmad Tejan Kabbah of the SLPP won the presidency, marking a crucial return to constitutional governance despite ongoing active war across rural provinces.

title: AFRC Military Coup and Junta Rule
summary: Major Johnny Paul Koroma seized power, forming an alliance between AFRC and RUF forces.
description: Major Johnny Paul Koroma overthrew President Kabbah in May 1997, inviting the RUF to join the Armed Forces Revolutionary Council (AFRC) junta. President Kabbah fled to Guinea. In February 1998, ECOMOG peacekeeping forces commanded by Nigerian General Maxwell Khobe ousted the junta and restored Kabbah's legitimate government to Freetown.

title: Signing of the Lomé Peace Agreement
summary: Government and RUF signed a peace framework in Togo, providing controversial amnesties and leading to UNAMSIL deployment.
description: Following six weeks of negotiations in Lomé, Togo, President Kabbah and RUF leader Foday Sankoh signed the Lomé Peace Agreement. The accord granted controversial blanket amnesty for war atrocities and appointed Sankoh head of the Commission for the Management of Strategic Resources, National Reconstruction and Development. It established UNAMSIL peacekeepers to enforce disarmament.

title: Official End of the Civil War & Freetown Declaration
summary: President Kabbah symbolically burned weapons in Lungi, declaring 'the war is over' after disarming over 75,000 fighters.
description: Following extensive disarmament supported by UNAMSIL peacekeepers and British military intervention, President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah officially declared the civil war over on 18 January 2002 during a ceremonial bonfire of weapons at Lungi. Over 75,000 ex-combatants had surrendered weapons, opening the path for post-conflict reconstruction and justice mechanisms.

title: Establishment of TRC and Special Court for Sierra Leone
summary: Dual transitional justice model created: Truth & Reconciliation Commission and UN-backed Special Court.
description: Sierra Leone pioneered a dual transitional justice architecture. The Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) documented conflict causes and published its comprehensive report in 2004. Concurrently, the Special Court for Sierra Leone (SCSL), an independent hybrid tribunal, indicted 13 key figures, including Liberian President Charles Taylor and CDF commander Hinga Norman, for war crimes and crimes against humanity.

title: Outbreak of Ebola Virus Disease Epidemic
summary: The deadliest Ebola outbreak in history affected Sierra Leone, claiming 3,956 lives.
description: On 25 May 2014, Sierra Leone confirmed its first case of Ebola Virus Disease in Kailahun District near the Guinean border. The epidemic spread rapidly, placing immense strain on healthcare infrastructure and public safety. Over 14,124 confirmed and suspected cases were recorded, with 3,956 deaths, before WHO declared Sierra Leone free of Ebola transmission on 17 March 2016.

title: Regent Mudslide and Flooding Disaster
summary: Catastrophic mudslide at Mount Sugar Loaf killed over 1,100 people and displaced thousands in Freetown.
description: Following heavy torrential rainfall, a massive section of Mount Sugar Loaf collapsed at Regent on the outskirts of Freetown. The resulting avalanche of mud and debris swept through informal settlements along the Lumley Creek valley, claiming an estimated 1,141 lives and displacing over 3,000 residents, drawing critical focus to urban planning and climate resilience.

title: Election of President Julius Maada Bio & Launch of Free Quality School Education
summary: Julius Maada Bio was elected president, launching the Free Quality School Education (FQSE) program.
description: Following a competitive two-round election, Julius Maada Bio of the SLPP defeated Samura Kamara of the APC to win the presidency. In August 2018, President Bio launched his administration's flagship Free Quality School Education (FQSE) initiative, paying tuition fees and providing learning materials for over two million primary and secondary school pupils nationwide.

title: 2023 General Elections & Cross-Party National Dialogue Agreement
summary: Presidential elections conducted and follow-up peace dialogue mediated by ECOWAS and the Commonwealth.
description: Sierra Leone held general elections on 24 June 2023, where Chief Electoral Commissioner Mohamed Konneh announced President Julius Maada Bio re-elected for a second term. Following political opposition disputes regarding electoral tabulation transparency, ECOWAS, African Union, and Commonwealth facilitators mediated a cross-party Agreement for National Unity in October 2023 between the ruling SLPP and opposition APC to reform electoral institutions.
